title: Labor for Palestine National Network Solidarity with the Palestinian Trade Union Call for Global Action November 20-29, 2026
content:
Solidarity with the Palestinian Trade Union Call for Global Action November 20-29, 2026

The Labor for Palestine National Network stands in full solidarity with the Palestinian labor movement’s urgent call for global action to end complicity in Israel’s ongoing genocide and apartheid, from Friday, November 20, 2026 leading up to the International Day of Solidarity with the Palestinian People on Sunday, November 29, 2026.

As the Palestinian labor call points out:

“Our struggle for justice in Palestine is inseparable from the global struggle against systemic racism, exploitation, climate devastation and all forms of oppression.

“It is the duty of unions to ensure that the workers they represent—whether in ports, on ships, in businesses, or in government offices—are not involved, often without their knowledge and/or consent, in actions that involve complicity in atrocity crimes anywhere, including Israel’s war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide against our people.”

Zionism is racism, and both the Democratic and Republican parties have blood on their hands for their deep complicity in Israeli settler colonialism, demonizing Palestinian resistance, and attacking the Palestine solidarity movement.

Although US workers have the power to end bipartisan-backed Israeli genocide, US labor leadership, which is closely tied to the Democratic Party establishment, has been deeply complicit with Zionism for more than a century, and most unions have—at best—remained silent.

Major unions who have nominally called for a ceasefire and arms embargo fail to acknowledge the Palestinan trade union calls or the Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions (BDS) picketline, and continue to resist members’ demands to use workers’ power—at the workplace, in the electoral arena, and in the streets—to shut down the genocide down, which continues to grind on with no end in sight.

This breach of solidarity was conspicuous during the historic October 30, 2026 international dockworker strike in solidarity with Palestine, which shut down 113 ports in five continents and 22 countries—none of them in the US—and now again during November’s week of global actions.

The indifference of union officialdom is a betrayal of the most basic labor principle, “An Injury to One Is an Injury to All.” As the Palestinian General Federation of Trade Unions-Gaza reminded US unions in 2025: “True labor solidarity is demonstrated through actions, not just words, and we count on your awareness and determination to take concrete steps to end this tragedy.”

Now is the time to reaffirm and escalate more than a half-century of rank-and-file labor solidarity with Palestine, including groundbreaking statements by the League of Revolutionary Black Workers in 1969, Arab worker-led strikes and protests against the UAW leadership’s support for Israel in 1973, ILWU dockers’ refusal to handle Israeli Zim Line vessels since 2014, the UAW’s 2026 divestment from Israel Bonds, and other grassroots Palestine labor solidarity since 2023.

As the November 21 Bay Area Mobilization for Palestine and Against War points out:

“This call to action comes at the heels of the US midterm elections, when voters this month delivered a strong rejection of US support for Israel and its genocide in Gaza, the war on Iran, the militarized brutality of ICE, and Trump’s racist and authoritarian agenda. Our movement has made clear that Palestinian liberation is inseparable from all struggles against racism, exploitation, and oppression everywhere. Let’s mobilize to show the people of Palestine our unwavering support, and to amplify to those in power what people everywhere are demanding: Stop Arming Israel, and No to War on Iran!”

In solidarity with the Palestinian trade union call, we support:

Strikes, walkouts, rallies, teach-ins, and protests at schools, colleges and universities in solidarity with the November 20 International Youth Strike Against War.

Direct action, withholding labor, and other forms of solidarity throughout the week of November 20-27, including a focus on Black Friday, November 27, to stop arming Israel and end the genocide.

From the River to the Sea, Palestine Will Be Free!

Why is Palestine a Labor Issue?

An injury to one is an injury to all. The Israeli settler-colonial regime is part of the same U.S.-backed system of racist state violence that brutalizes Black, Indigenous, African, Arab, Middle Eastern, Muslim, Asian, and working class people in the Global South and around the world. With Israel’s knee on their neck, Palestinians can’t breathe, and we unconditionally stand with them, just as they have stood with our struggles for Black and Brown Lives, Standing Rock, migrant rights, and beyond.

Our tax dollars fund Israel. Israel’s crimes are committed with tens of billions in bipartisan US weaponry—tax dollars that should be spent instead to reverse Israeli destruction in Palestine, and on badly-needed jobs, food, housing, healthcare, education, and transportation for poor and working people at home.

Our workplaces arm Israel. Many of our unionized factories, logistics, academia, tech, and other workplaces—without our consent—produce weapons, transportation, research, technology, and other materials for the genocidal Israeli regime.

Our unions fund Israel. Our unions are already involved—on the wrong side. In the 1920s-1930s, top labor officials donated millions to the Histadrut, the Zionist labor federation that spearheaded anti-Palestinian dispossession, apartheid, and ethnic cleansing, including the Nakba (Catastrophe) that established the Israeli state in 1948. For more than 70 years, they have used our union dues and pension funds to buy billions of dollars worth of Israel Bonds. Today, despite horrendous Palestinian casualties, most labor officials remain silent—or worse.

Global working class solidarity is the only way to win. More than ever, in this era of globalization, workers and oppressed people everywhere are up a common enemy. We can’t win if we are atomized by union, or even country. We need international, classwide unity. That means every worker must take on the task of building solidarity with Palestine—today an epicenter of class struggle.

Workers can stop Israeli genocide. More than 50 years ago, Arab and Black auto workers led a wildcat strike and other actions to protest UAW complicity with Israel. Today, we can follow their example in respecting the Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions (BDS) picket line by protesting, bringing union resolutions, and—above all—by mobilizing our collective power at the workplace, as shown by dockers in South Africa, India, Sweden, Norway, Turkey, Italy, Belgium, and the ILWU on the West Coast of the United States, which has respected Block the Boat’s community-labor picket line by refusing to handle Israeli cargo.

title: Statement — IOF OFF REKOGNITION (Amazon Worker Intifada)
content:
A post shared by Amazon Worker Intifada (@amznworkerintifada)

IOF OFF REKOGNITION. Amazon cannot claim neutrality while its technology is being used to surveil, track, and identify Palestinians under “israeli” genocide and occupation.

Read our Statement 🔗Statement: [awi.ac/statement]

The revelations about Amazon Rekognition and the processing and identification of millions of Palestinian faces in photographs expose what workers, shareholders, and communities have been warning about for years: Amazon technology is not neutral when it becomes infrastructure for “israeli” genocide and occupation.

We are the workers who build, maintain, and support these systems. We did not consent to our labor being used to facilitate “israeli” surveillance, displacement, and genocide of Palestinians. And we refuse to stay silent.

We demand that Amazon: * Stop selling facial recognition technology to Israel. * Launch an independent, transparent investigation into the use of Rekognition and AWS by the IOF and ICE. * Guarantee workers the right to speak out without fear of retaliation about the article and petition.

Our labor is not consent. Our technology should not be a digital weapon of an ongoing “israeli” genocide in Gaza and occupation of Palestine. Sign the Petition. 🔗 Petition: [awi.ac/petition]

On Nov 16, 2026, the Guardian revealed that the IOF uploaded 3.5 million photographs of Palestinians to Amazon’s cloud, AWS, to be processed through Amazon Rekognition, the company’s facial recognition AI service. These included photographs from Rolling Stone, the IOF’s central database of Palestinians stored on AWS, which has amassed millions of photographs taken from identity cards issued to every Palestinian resident when they turn 16.

Following the ground invasion of Gaza, the IOF deployed facial recognition systems at checkpoints where Palestinians were being forcibly displaced and fleeing the IOF’s bombardment. IOF used AWS infrastructure to support the processing of images collected at these checkpoints, matching people against photographs held in Rolling Stone.

Any suggestion that Amazon is merely a passive or neutral technology provider, detached from the military operations its infrastructure supports, is impossible to reconcile with these revelations. Amazon is the digital arms manufacturer of the “israeli” genocide in Gaza.

In Oct 2025, The Intercept revealed multiple documents showing that the “israeli” Ministry of Defense had purchased access to Rekognition for an intelligence project run by the military’s Central Command. As workers, we understood what it meant when Amazon sold facial recognition technology to an occupation military carrying out a genocide. We did not need the Guardian to tell us what the IOF would use it for.

None of this should come as a surprise. Amazon has been warned, repeatedly, by their workers, by their shareholders, and by the community.

This is not the first time Amazon has been exposed for selling Rekognition to a customer that uses it against a civilian population without their consent.

In 2018, the ACLU demonstrated that Rekognition misidentified Black and Brown members of Congress as criminal suspects. Washington County, Oregon, and the Orlando Police Department ran pilots. Federal agencies piloted it too.

Then came June 2020. Weeks after a Minneapolis police officer killed George Floyd, as an uprising swept the streets against police violence and Big Tech’s surveillance of protesters, Amazon announced a one-year moratorium on police use of Rekognition. A year later, it extended the ban indefinitely.

But the moratorium applied only to police departments conducting criminal investigations. It never covered ICE, which AWS executives pitched Rekognition to in 2018, and whose biometric backbone — the IDENT database, containing records on hundreds of millions of people — is hosted on AWS. It never covered the FBI, which Justice Department documents in 2024 showed was planning to use Rekognition to mass-process seized devices. It never covered Palantir, whose technology, in its own words, ‘is used on occasion to kill people.’ Palantir has also sold its AI services to the IOF for use against Palestinians, holds over $150 million in ICE contracts, and runs its deportation-case software entirely on AWS servers.

Amazon threw us a moratorium bone to keep us quiet, while slithering behind the scenes to sell Rekognition to bigger customers further up the chain. The ban protects people facing American police. It never protected Palestinians facing an occupying military. The same company that decided its software was too dangerous for a city police department in 2020 spent 2023 and 2024 migrating the IOF’s databases into a segregated, fortified “walled garden” for military and intelligence data, with a plan to migrate “pictures, videos, all the confidential intelligence information — everything.”

Amazon’s actions treat Palestinian lives as expendable: people to be surveilled, their identities stored, and their lives subjected to genocidal military violence by the IOF.

The IOF’s facial recognition of Palestinians has been operating for years in the West Bank. Blue Wolf allows IOF soldiers to photograph Palestinians using a phone app and pull up their files. It gamifies the collection of Palestinian faces, with the IOF competing to photograph the most people, children included, and receiving prizes and rewards for the highest rankings. Red Wolf uses facial recognition cameras at checkpoints in Hebron to scan Palestinians, identify them against military databases, and inform soldiers whether they are permitted to pass, should be questioned, or are due for arrest. The system can also enroll previously unregistered faces without people’s knowledge or consent, expanding its database of Palestinian biometric data. Amnesty International has documented these systems and called them automated apartheid. The Guardian’s sources confirm that Rolling Stone’s photo archive, the same archive now stored on AWS, has routinely fed these facial recognition programmes.

Palestinians are forced into this system as children. At 16, the occupation photographs you for your ID card. From that day on, every aspect of your life becomes part of your file in Rolling Stone: where you go, who your family is, what you own, whether you have been flagged. Nothing is private for a Palestinian. And now that file itself lives on Amazon’s servers, inside a walled garden Amazon built for the IOF’s military and intelligence data.

This data feeds the “israeli” AI algorithms — Lavender, Where’s Daddy, and their kin — that mark Palestinian families for IOF murder. When the data outgrew the military’s own servers, the IOF turned to AWS and its “endless storage.” The living Palestinian inherits this file at every checkpoint, every permit application, every bombing cycle. There is no dignity afforded to Palestinians. There is capture, storage, death, suffering, and profit.

AWS’s Responsible AI policy prohibits using its services to:

“violate the privacy rights of others, including unlawful tracking, monitoring, and identification”

“harass, harm, or encourage the harm of individuals or specific groups”

AWS’s Acceptable Use Policy prohibits using its services to:

“threaten, incite, promote, or actively encourage violence”

For years, Amazon told its shareholders that “AWS will suspend or terminate access to Amazon Rekognition if we determine a customer is violating our AUP [Acceptable Use Policy] or the AWS legal terms.”

Amazon’s assurances about enforcing its own policies are now impossible to take at face value. Amazon has acknowledged that its customer, the IOF, was using Rekognition to process millions of photographs of Palestinians, while its own policies prohibit unlawful surveillance, violations of privacy, and harm to individuals and groups. Yet Amazon has offered no meaningful public explanation of how this use was assessed, whether it was investigated, or why its policies were not enforced. The IOF’s use of Rekognition, as the Guardian’s revelations make clear, violates each of these policies. The Guardian also revealed in October last year that the Nimbus contract prohibits Amazon from restricting, suspending, or withdrawing services to “israel” — even if “israel” breaches Amazon’s own terms of service. The enforcement mechanism Amazon held up as its conscience was sold off in advance.

What is the point of a corporate human rights policy if a company has contractually surrendered its ability to enforce it against one of its most important customers?

Amazon’s own shareholders have tried to force an answer for six years. Since 2020, resolutions calling for an independent investigation into how customers use Rekognition and other AWS services have been submitted six times, winning upwards of 40 percent support — a level that typically forces a meaningful corporate response. In 2026, Amazon petitioned the SEC to block the resolution from a vote on a loophole technicality, and won.

Amazon says it had “no visibility” into how the IOF used its cloud. The IOF informed Amazon of the 3.5 million photo upload. The Ministry of Defense’s purchases of Rekognition are documented. The walled garden was built to Amazon’s own specifications, as a contractual obligation. The IOF didn’t just use AWS — IOF soldiers worked inside it, on the 28th floor of AWS’s Tel Aviv offices, exploring how to run the Gaza facial recognition programme on AWS. A workload scanning millions of faces at this scale, requiring a business justification for high throughput, runs through checks Amazon itself mandates. Make no mistake: this was visible, lucratively visible, to Amazon.

We are the workers who built, maintain, and support the Amazon technology that serves as the technological backbone of an ongoing “israeli” genocide in Gaza. We did not consent to our labor being used for this. We never will.

The Guardian’s revelations are just the tip of the iceberg. Amazon’s collaboration in the genocide runs deep. We demand that Amazon:

Stop Selling Facial Recognition Technology to “israel”: End all sales of Rekognition to “israel” to prevent its continued use in the ongoing genocide in Gaza and the occupation and apartheid in Palestine.

Conduct an Investigation: Conduct and release the results of a transparent, independent investigation of how Amazon customers, including “israel” and ICE, are using Rekognition in violation of international human rights law, the AWS Responsible AI Policy, and the AWS Acceptable use Policy.

Protect Worker Speech: Guarantee zero retaliation — no suspension, firing, or harassment — for any worker who wants to discuss or engage in moral discourse about the Guardian article or this petition on internal platforms like Slack or email.

We will continue to organize, speak out, and escalate until these demands are met.

title: Amazon Workers Call on Amazon to Stop Scanning Palestinian Children (Amazon Worker Intifada)
content:
This petition was written by Amazon workers and shared internally on Nov 16, 2026 in response to The Guardian’s revelations of Amazon Rekognition’s complicity in ongoing the “israeli” genocide in Gaza.

Sign Worker Petition Sign Public Petition

The Guardian has revealed that “israel” uploaded 3.5 million photos of Palestinians into Amazon’s cloud to be run through AWS Rekognition, the company’s facial recognition technology. The photos include the ID photos “israel” forces every Palestinian to take at 16. After the ground invasion in Gaza, the IOF aimed this system at its own checkpoints, where cameras scanned Palestinians as they fled “israeli” bombing and matched their faces against Rolling Stone, described by an IOF soldier as the system “where all the information relevant to the control of the Palestinian civilian population is centralised”. A military IOF source said Amazon’s cloud was used precisely because of the “very large scale” of images collected at those checkpoints, which became sites of mass detention and enforced disappearance, as documented by UN bodies.

Under Project Nimbus, the company constructed a segregated, fortified “walled garden” inside its Tel Aviv data centers for IOF military and intelligence data, and hosted IOF soldiers at its own offices in “israel” as they explored how to run the Gaza facial recognition programme on AWS. Rolling Stone’s plan, in the words of a military source, was to migrate “pictures, videos, all the confidential intelligence information — everything.”

Since October 2023, “israel” has carried out a sustained bombardment that has caused daily suffering and the murder of countless Palestinians, enforced a deliberate starvation blockade, continued bombing Gaza despite the so-called “ceasefire”, and damaged or destroyed 82% of all structures, including schools and hospitals. Behind this carnage, Amazon serves as the technological backbone of “israel’s” surveillance and bombing apparatus in Gaza.

Through contracts like Projects Nimbus and Sirius, Amazon facilitates A.I. targeting systems that use mass amounts of surveillance data to identify and strike Palestinian civilians. When data volumes, including billions of audio files, exceeded military server capacity, the IOF turned to Amazon Web Services (AWS) and its “endless storage” for information on almost “everyone” in Gaza. IOF personnel testified that data stored in Amazon’s cloud was used to confirm aerial assassination strikes, many firing munitions from “israel”-owned weapons firms that Amazon has sold cloud and A.I. services to throughout the genocide.

In June 2025, a UN report formally categorized Amazon, Google, and Microsoft as part of a “joint criminal enterprise” actively transforming colonial occupation into genocide by providing “israel’s” essential tech and A.I. infrastructure. By September 2025, Microsoft was exposed storing 11,500 terabytes of intercepted Palestinian phone calls for Unit 8200 on Azure, and the IOF swiftly planned to move the trove to AWS. A month later, it was revealed that as part of Project Nimbus, Amazon and “israel” agreed to a secret “winking” mechanism: coded payments that alert “israel” of any incoming legal demands or investigations from foreign governments for “israeli” data. Similar to Microsoft, Amazon has engineered a scheme to buy the IOF time to move evidence of its genocide hosted in AWS.

Amazon Rekognition is just one tool in the digital arsenal powering “israel’s” ongoing genocide of Gaza.

While the Guardian leak is abhorrent, it should not be shocking. It is not the first time Amazon has knowingly profited off of human rights abuses using Rekognition facial A.I. technology.

In 2018, the ACLU revealed that Amazon was selling Rekognition to U.S. police departments despite its documented racial bias that frequently misidentified Black and Brown members of Congress as criminal suspects. During the George Floyd protests in 2020, there was public outcry about police use of facial recognition technology to surveil protestors. Facing public and shareholder pressure, Amazon announced a one-year moratorium on sales to local law enforcement, later extending it “indefinitely”.

Despite the moratorium, Amazon continued to pitch and sell Rekognition to federal entities like ICE and the FBI, cementing its position as “the largest provider of facial recognition technology to U.S. law enforcement, including federal immigration agencies and the FBI.” ICE now uses facial recognition to scan individuals on the street without consent, instantly checking their immigration status against federal databases to identify targets for detention and deportation. This surveillance infrastructure has already been used against Amazon’s own workers: ICE detained two Amazon Flex drivers at the company’s Hazel Park, Michigan facility in February 2026.

Now, the same infrastructure used to surveil and deport migrants in the U.S. is being leveraged to target and murder Palestinians in Gaza. Amazon did not learn from the police scandal; they simply moved up the chain of command, finding new markets here and in Palestine for the same dangerous facial A.I. technology.

Amazon has imposed a moratorium on Rekognition sales to U.S. police before; we demand similar restrictions on “israel”. We did not consent to building the tools used to murder Palestinians, and we refuse to stay silent any longer. Therefore, we demand that Amazon:

Stop Selling Facial Recognition Technology to “israel”: End all sales of Rekognition to “israel” to prevent its continued use in the ongoing genocide in Gaza and the occupation and apartheid in Palestine.

Conduct an Investigation: Conduct and release the results of a transparent, independent investigation of how Amazon customers, including “israel” and ICE, are using Rekognition in violation of international human rights law, the AWS Responsible AI Policy, and the AWS Acceptable use Policy.

Protect Worker Speech: Guarantee zero retaliation—no suspension, firing, or harassment—for any worker who wants to discuss or engage in moral discourse about the Guardian article or this petition on internal platforms like Slack or email.

We, the workers, made these demands before. In May 2021, after “israel” murdered more than 250 Palestinians in Gaza, more than 500 of us wrote to Andy Jassy and Jeff Bezos demanding Amazon cut all ties with “israel” and protect pro-Palestinian speech. That October, 300 workers sent a petition to the executives demanding Amazon pull out of the Nimbus contract and cut all ties with the IOF. Amazon ignored both. In 2023, after “israel” began its genocidal onslaught in Gaza, 1,700 of us again demanded Amazon cancel its contracts with the IOF. Again, silence.

This time, our petition comes from an organized Amazon worker resistance movement—and for the fourth time, we are here because Andy Jassy (Amazon CEO) and Matt Garman (AWS CEO) are murdering Palestinians with our labor, all while expecting us to remain silent. They are not alone. The leaders of Rekognition—Peter DeSantis (SVP), Vishal Sharma (VP), Srini Veeravanallur (Director), Helbert Fonseca Maich (Senior Manager), and Palak Mehta (Senior Manager)—authorize the sign-offs, the high server capacities, and the shipment of Rekognition code to the IOF. We will continue to escalate until all our demands are met. We want material change, and we want it now.

title: Trump Subpoenas Teachers Union for Info on Pro-Palestine Students (The Intercept)
content:
The expansive subpoena asked the American Federation of Teachers headquarters for information related to a vandalism case against Michigan students.

Activists gather at a pro-Palestine encampment at the University of Michigan’s campus on April 24, 2024, in Ann Arbor, Michigan.Photo: Adam J. Dewey/Anadolu via Getty Images

The Trump administration quietly broadened its crackdown on campus pro-Palestine protests over the summer, moving to ensnare one of the largest unions in the country in a case revolving around alleged incidents of vandalism.

The national headquarters of the American Federation of Teachers, or AFT, received a grand jury subpoena in August as part of an ongoing federal investigation into protests at the University of Michigan. Twelve pro-Palestine activists have been charged with felonies in the case.

The subpoena against the AFT, which has not been previously reported and was obtained by The Intercept, shows the administration casting a wider net in its investigation into student protesters than was previously known.

“They’re using this language around conspiracy and trying to draw in all of these different organizations.”

The Graduate Employees’ Organization, or GEO, an AFT local at the university, also received a notice to provide information and testimony to a grand jury around the same time, according to a copy of the previously unreported subpoena obtained by The Intercept.

The effort to draw a powerful, liberal union into a case that revolves around spray-painting charges represents a dramatic escalation in Donald Trump’s war on the left.

“They’re using this language around conspiracy and trying to draw in all of these different organizations that are taking stances against fascism, against the government, and anything that’s counter to their ideology,” said Natalie Chen, who serves as GEO’s communications director. “This is perhaps another ‘in’ for them to broaden their attack

As pro-Palestine protests swept campuses across the country in 2024 and widespread demonstration broke out against U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement this year, the Trump administration has sought to paint left-of-center protest, nonprofit work, and labor organizing as a nefarious far-left conspiracy, even labeling some activists and groups as terrorists.

Critics of the administration’s crackdown on Palestine solidarity and protests against ICE see moves like the ones against AFT and GEO as part of an effort to silence dissent.

“Historically, federal grand jury subpoenas have been used against social movements and political dissent to gather information, to isolate individuals, and of course to try and prosecute people,” said Xavier de Janon, executive director of the National Lawyers Guild. “What is different in politicized cases is the extent of people and places that get subpoenaed, which many people see clearly goes way beyond what they’re supposedly trying to prosecute.”

Activists at the University of Michigan said the effort to extract information about students from the union was an attempt to further target pro-Palestine protesters and their relationships with labor organizers.

“What is different in politicized cases is the extent of people and places that get subpoenaed.”

The grand jury subpoenas came as part of a case that has seen a dozen protesters become caught up in serious federal charges against the students, dubbed “the Michigan 12.” They allege that protesters committed illegal acts like vandalism as part of a pressure campaign seeking to push university officials to divest school holdings tied to the Israeli genocide in Palestine.

The subpoenas against the GEO and AFT were requested by federal prosecutor Margaret Smith with assistance from FBI agent Kara Phipps — two federal officials deeply enmeshed in the investigation into the Michigan 12. (The Department of Justice declined to comment for this story.)

The subpoenas were issued as the GEO was already reeling after its president, Hiab Teshome, was charged with felony embezzlement by local prosecutors working in conjunction with the University of Michigan Police Department.

Authorities alleged that Teshome, who was a bargaining team member in the middle of intense contract negotiations between the union and the school, misused organizational funds to purchase laptops for a campus club.

In a statement, the GEO called the charges meritless and characterized them as an attempt to limit protected union activity. Teshome was later cleared of any wrongdoing by the university’s student government, and the charges against her were thrown out by a judge.

Federal prosecutors issued the subpoenas the same day the charges against Teshome were dismissed, leaving activists little time to regroup.

Although GEO is not mentioned in the federal indictment against protesters, the AFT chapter is a prominent member of the Tahrir coalition, a pro-Palestine student collective that is referenced repeatedly in federal filings and characterized by prosecutors as having ties with defendants.

The scope of the information requested of the unions by the federal government is broad. GEO and AFT are being compelled, according to the subpoenas, to surrender information including complete membership rolls, payroll records on officers, reimbursement policies, audit reports, and all transcribed minutes on membership and executive board meetings of the University of Michigan local since January 2023.

The American Federation of Teachers has more than 1.7 million members and more than 3,000 local chapters.

After receiving the subpoena, GEO immediately obtained attorneys and filed a motion to quash the order. The national office of the AFT, however, has not publicly acknowledged receiving the directive or stated whether it intends to comply. (AFT did not respond to requests for comment about the subpoenas, including whether the union would be complying.)

Teshome, the GEO president, believes that the subpoena against the AFT may be an attempt by the federal government to circumvent the local union and force the national organization to comply.

“GEO has taken the stance that we will do everything in our power to protect the data and the information of our membership,” Teshome said. “I think that this is a strategy that the federal government is using in order to try to actually receive the information that they are trying to get by usurping us as a local union and going instead to AFT national.”

Additionally, Teshome likened the GEO’s case to similar surveillance activities conducted by federal agents against trade unionists in Minnesota as part of the Trump White House’s National Security Presidential Memorandum-7, a presidential directive that attempts to criminalize leftist political organizations.

“All of the repression we are seeing across the country is the federal government’s attack on anyone who has political thought,” Teshome said. “Michigan is no different than all of these other cases in that we are one of the testing grounds for NSPM-7 and how much oppression can be applied through the federal government in order to demobilize and disorganize.

title: The U.S. government is escalating its attack on Palestine activism in Michigan (Mondoweiss)
content:
Four more pro-Palestine activists have been indicted on “conspiracy” charges stemming from protests at the University of Michigan, bringing the total to 12. The defendants now face sentences ranging from five years to several decades.

By Yarden Azoulay Katz and Adi Saleem November 10, 2026

FBI agent stopping and searching a vehicle in Ann Arbor, MI as part of the crackdown on new defendants, October 29, 2026.

The U.S. government is expanding its assault on Palestine solidarity activism in Michigan. Last summer, the FBI conducted raids against pro-Palestine activists connected to the University of Michigan. The defendants, known as the Michigan 8, were indicted by the Department of Justice on “conspiracy” charges, specifically “conspiracy to transmit threats in interstate and foreign commerce” and “conspiracy to intimidate a witness.” On Thursday, October 29, the FBI raided the home of activists in the same circle. The next day, the government unsealed a superseding indictment that adds four more defendants to the case, turning the Michigan 8 into the Michigan 12.

The four new defendants are all recent graduates of the University of Michigan with ties to campus Palestine activism. Like the initial eight defendants, they are charged with conspiracy and potentially face long prison sentences, from five years to several decades.

The federal government’s new indictment doubles down on previous allegations of “antisemitism.” In a press release announcing the indictment, U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of Michigan Jerome F. Gorgon, Jr. claims the defendants aimed “to terrorize our Jewish community” and even compares them to Hitler and the biblical Pharaoh. The government again portrays the defendants as “terrorists” because of their alleged support for Palestinian resistance groups, despite never charging any defendant with “terrorism,” “hate crimes,” or even “vandalism.”

As part of this attack, the government filed an emergency motion to detain one of the initial eight defendants (who had been released on bond) all the way until trial. In recent months, FBI agents have also made visits to the homes of several Palestine activists in southeast Michigan.

This new wave of repression and propaganda is intended to send chills through the Palestine solidarity movement and sway public opinion against the defendants. But community supporters, family, and friends of the Michigan 12 are continuing to fight back.

On October 29, Henry David Mackeen-Shapiro (who goes by Drin Shapiro) was heading home from the Detroit public school where he teaches. Shapiro was stopped by FBI agents who had their guns pointed at him, with about six police vehicles present. They arrested him and seized his car and phone.

Around an hour later, about fifteen FBI agents arrived at Shapiro’s home. They knocked on the door, announcing they had a search warrant but refusing to show it, according to one person who was present for the entire raid. Those inside the house decided to open the door to avoid having the agents break through it (as they have done in the June 2026 and April 2025 raids on local Palestine activists). As the search began, two agents were stationed outside, pointing their rifles at the house windows, while another agent with a rifle guarded the door.

The agents conducting the search made clear to those present that if they stay in the house, they must remain put and not follow the agents. The agents soon received a message on their radio devices asking them to turn off their body cameras; they later confirmed to the residents that they have done so. The agents refused additional requests to show a warrant, only leaving it on the kitchen table when the search was over. The warrant instructs the agents to seize devices that may contain communications with several other Michigan 12 defendants (the agents took Shapiro’s computer).https://archive.org/embed/fbiagents-seizing-materials-drin-shapiro-home-oct-29-2026

FBI agents exiting defendants’ Detroit home after the raid, carrying a box with seized materials, October 29, 2026. Video by the Michigan 12 defense effort.

“It was a really unjust process,” a person present during the raid said. “I was not told what was happening, I was not told my rights, and I was not shown a warrant.” That the agents turned off their body cameras made it obvious the government is acting with “a total lack of transparency,” they added.

Shapiro spent the night in jail and was arraigned the next day in Detroit federal court, where he was released on $10,000 unsecured bond with similar conditions to those of his co-defendants, including restrictions on travel and wearing a GPS ankle monitor for which he must cover the costs.

On the day of the Detroit home raid, FBI agents searched Ann Arbor for a newly indicted defendant in the case, Aaron VonBargen. The agents ended up detaining and searching VonBargen’s younger sibling, Eric Ming VonBargen. “As I was walking to my car after class, multiple unmarked vehicles cornered me and about a dozen FBI agents proceeded to search and detain me. It wasn’t until minutes in that they asked for my name, and only then did they realized I was not my sibling, who is several years older,” VonBargen said in a November 3 statement published by the Michigan 12 defense effort. “By the time I was released, my car and backpack were already thrown apart.” The following morning, Eric’s sibling, Aaron VonBargen, turned themselves in. They were also released on unsecured bond with similar conditions to Shapiro’s.

The agent who detained Eric Ming VanBargen has been attending multiple court proceedings in the Michigan 12 case. The authors witnessed him sitting next to and speaking with Ryan Cavanaugh, a Sergeant Detective with the University of Michigan Police (UMPD) who has a long record of going after local Palestine solidarity activists. Cavanaugh has also been speaking in court with the government’s attorney, and UMPD, which participated in the June 2026 raid on the initial eight defendants, alongside the FBI. While the University of Michigan has officially remained silent regarding the case, it is clearly aiding the Trump administration’s crackdown.

Following the raid on Shapiro’s home, on November 2, U.S. Attorney Maggie Smith filed an emergency motion to revoke the bond of Zainab Hakim, one of the original eight defendants, and jail her until the trial. The November 2 motion alleges that Hakim, who was present during the raid and lives with Shapiro (who is her boyfriend), damaged his computer to prevent seizure. Yet the government also used the motion to promote bigger allegations of antisemitism, revealing the absurdity of their case.

The motion attacks a statement made by the judge on the case, Judith E. Levy, who had stated in a September 2026 bond hearing that there is nothing to suggest Hakim is anti-Jewish. “There’s nothing that’s happened over the last two months or maybe last year or anytime I’ve seen, there’s nothing in the indictment, there’s nothing in any of this material that would indicate that that’s the case,” concluded Levy, who is Jewish and the daughter of a child survivor of the Nazi Holocaust.

To argue against Levy’s conclusion, U.S. Attorney Smith – who wears a large cross necklace to court – presented what are allegedly encrypted messages between Hakim, who is Muslim, and her co-defendant Shapiro, who is Jewish. The two appear to be discussing chants that could be used at protests against the genocide in Palestine. Smith claims that this is merely one example of Hakim and Shapiro’s “many conversations regarding their antisemitic feelings,” and supposedly evidence of their risk to the “Jewish community.”

It’d be hard to make up a more ridiculous scenario: a Christian prosecutor with strongly Zionist views arguing against the Jewish judge’s call that there’s no trace of antisemitism by showing that a Muslim woman and her Jewish boyfriend are resisting Zionism together. The only “antisemitic” thing here is the government’s premise that the Zionist organizations aiding it (such as the Jewish Federation of Detroit) speak for all Jews – and that the safety of Jews requires the settler-colonial brutality of Israel.

In the October 30 press release announcing the new indictment, Smith’s superior, U.S. Attorney Jerome F. Gorgon, Jr., also framed the case as a heroic mission to defend Jews:

“These alleged attempts to terrorize our Jewish community and government officials are nothing new. From Pharaoh to Hitler to Hamas, those who terrorize Jews have been the bad guys. As Americans, our job is to fight the bad guys.”

On November 3, the initial eight defendants were re-arraigned in Judge Levy’s courtroom based on the superseding indictment, which resulted in the same bond conditions.

In the same court session, Judge Levy also considered defendant Ahmet Korkaya’s motion to remove the curfew and GPS ankle monitoring from his bond conditions. U.S. Attorney Smith argued against the motion, again invoking Jewish safety. “I can tell you, and as the Court knows, [that] being a member of the Jewish community automatically puts them on edge and at risk [of the defendant],” Smith said. Judge Levy was not persuaded and granted Korkaya’s motion, citing the Bail Reform Act, which calls for “the least restrictive” conditions to be used when possible. Smith asked for 48 hours to appeal the decision, which the court granted, but the government abandoned the appeal and the requested bond conditions were removed.

During proceedings, an attorney for one of the Michigan 12 argued that Gorgon’s press release is an unethical attempt by the government to influence public opinion before the trial begins. Judge Levy agreed that the statement is “very concerning” and asked Smith’s office to consider “taking this [press release] off the government’s website” or at least “retracting this statement about Hitler and Pharaoh.”

The Michigan 12 defense effort and community members have continued to fight the charges. On October 30, 2026, Drin Shapiro and Aaron VonBargen were arraigned in a courtroom packed with supporters, signaling to everyone that the defendants do not stand alone. Most court proceedings so far have been well attended by supporters, who often had to be redirected to court overflow rooms.

During the November 3 proceedings, a large crowd also gathered for a rally outside the Ann Arbor federal court. Community members raised the Palestinian flag, served food, and prepared gift bags and cards for the defendants. A hearing on the government’s motion to revoke defendant Zainab Hakim’s bond is scheduled for November 18 and is also expected to be packed with Michigan 12 supporters.

Michigan Democratic Party politicians, however, have not shown much support for the defendants so far. Representative Rashida Tlaib and Amir Makled, a lawyer who had represented student activists criminalized over Palestine and was recently elected to the University of Michigan Board of Regents, have said little about the case. One of the defendants had worked on the campaign of Abdul El-Sayed, the recent winner of the Michigan senate race, but after the June 2026 FBI raid, a spokesperson for El-Sayed distanced themselves from her.

The Michigan 12 case resembles other cases where the government is using “conspiracy” charges to criminalize social movements, like the case of the Minnesota 15 anti-ICE organizers. All this repression is linked: U.S. Attorney Gorgon, who oversees the Michigan 12 case, also brought charges of “using interstate communications to transmit a threat” against those making anti-ICE comments online in Michigan. This is why organizers across defense campaigns have been joining forces. It’s essential to strengthen these grassroots efforts, given the powers we are up against.

title: The Teamsters’ Midterm Disaster (Joe Allen)
content:
The Teamsters’ Midterm Disaster

Despite a post-election effort to perfume up the performance of the Teamsters’ in the recent midterm elections, a string of high profile endorsements, many with the blessing of its General President Sean O’Brien went down to a thumping defeat. The historic ‘blue wave’ changed the color of the electoral map in the United States and raised political hopes for many people that a change in direction in the country is possible. Trump’s second term was a nightmare and saw a dramatic shift to the left by many working class people.

Liz Shuler, president of the sclerotic and long declining AFL-CIO captured some of this feeling when she boasted:

“This blue wave was union-made. The billionaires had the money in this election, but working people had the power. The people who make this country run issued a clear mandate last night. Speaking with a unified voice, workers demanded that their elected leaders fight to raise their wages and lower costs, expand access to health care and unions, hold billionaire CEOs accountable, and check the Trump administration’s attacks on their freedoms. The labor movement is ready to work with these newly elected members of Congress, governors and state legislators on a bold agenda to deliver real change for the working class.”

Whether workers get real change after many failed blue waves during the last twenty years, is another question, but can Sean O’Brien make the same claims as Shuler? With a necklace of far right creeps hung around the Teamsters’ neck going down to glorious defeat, most notably Greg Abbott in Texas and Vivek Ramaswamy in Ohio, it is hard to see how the Teamsters have any credibility with anyone, anywhere. It’s worth asking out loud a question that many people have asked privately, are the Teamsters trying to be the most hated union in the United States?

The Teamsters’ midterm disaster has been foretold for several years now. Soon after the Teamsters settled their overhyped 2023 contract with United Parcel Service (UPS), Sean O’Brien, the union’s General President elected in 2021, had a string of chummy meetings with far right political figures in Washington, D.C. with then Senator J.D. Vance and Missouri Senator Josh Hawley. O’Brien was then invited to Mar-a-Largo by then former President Donald for an amiable meeting and photo opportunity. Trump was then invited to the Teamsters’ headquarters in Washington. For all this outreach to the far right, O’Brien was rewarded with a prime time speaking slot at the 2024 Republican Convention.

From there, it just got worse, as documented by Current Affairs contributor Hank Kennedy in his article, Sean O’Brien Sold Labor to Trump, and Got Nothing:

Under O’Brien the Teamsters went on record supporting the president’s pick for Secretary of Labor, Lori Chavez DeRemer, and O’Brien himself wrote an op-ed calling her “The Pro-Worker Choice for Labor” in Compact. Under questioning, DeRemer admitted she no longer supported the section of the PRO Act weakening state anti-union right-to-work laws. This bothered O’Brien not a bit. On Fox, he said that he and his bosom buddy Josh Hawley were working on a version of the PRO Act that “may not include [a ban on right-to-work]” O’Brien seemed to say that right-to-work laws could be “what works” for certain states. At least, that’s how the vehemently anti-union National Right to Work Committee interpreted his remarks in a post on X.

DeRemer resigned in disgrace, but was a guest of Sean O’Brien, whom she called her “good friend,” at the recent Teamsters convention in Las Vegas.

The Teamsters didn’t formally endorse Trump or the Democratic presidential candidate Vice-President Kamala Harris, but the non-endorsement of Harris was seen as a victory by Trump. Speaking to reporters, Trump said of the Teamsters decision not to endorse a candidate: “It’s a great honor. They’re not going to endorse the Democrats. That’s a big thing.” Most people following union and Teamster politics saw it as a backhanded endorsement of Trump.

“Sean O’Brien is not the first Teamster leader to have endorsed right-wing politicians hostile to organized labor,” Kennedy argued. “The Teamsters endorsed Richard Nixon, Ronald Reagan, and George H.W. Bush, usually in a cynical effort to stave off federal investigations and indictments of corrupt leadership. As far as is known, there’s no such cloud hanging over O’Brien’s head. He walks this road to perdition under his own steam.”

Join Medium for free to get updates from this writer.Subscribe

O’Brien has popularized the slogan “Teamsters vs. Everybody” during his first term in office. It articulates the strange and insular world of the Teamsters. And, he means it. The Teamsters under O’Brien’s leadership, with a handful of local exceptions, has remained silent to aloof to hostile to the various campaigns — Palestine, anti-ICE, opposition to Elon Musk and DOGE and the War in Iran, widespread corruption and massive inequality — that created the tsunami toppled the Republican control of Congress and wrecked MAGA. Back in February, I tried to raise awareness about the Teamsters’ endorsements in the upcoming election after the Texas Teamsters endorsed Gov. Greg Abbott for reelection. I wrote:

Let’s be clear about Abbott: He has no redeeming qualities, nor does he support policies that benefit working-class people. In fact, it’s quite the opposite. He has a wide-ranging anti-working-class political agenda. He enthusiastically supports Texas’s near ban on abortion, or the so-called “Heartbeat Bill.” He supports school privatization and the death penalty. All of these issues are near and dear to the Christian Nationalist Right in Texas and the myriad of police and sheriff’s associations that support his reelection campaign.

Abbott, like Trump, revels in cruelty. In June 2023, the Texas Tribune reported:

In a week when parts of the state are getting triple-digit temperatures and weather officials urge Texans to stay cool and hydrated, Gov. Greg Abbott gave final approval to a law that will eliminate local rules mandating water breaks for construction workers. House Bill 2127 was passed by the Texas Legislature during this year’s regular legislative session. Abbott signed it Tuesday. It will go into effect on Sept. 1.

Texas is the state where the most workers die from high temperatures, government data shows. At least 42 workers died in Texas between 2011 and 2021 from environmental heat exposure, according to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. Workers’ unions claim this data doesn’t fully reflect the magnitude of the problem because heat-related deaths are often recorded under a different primary cause of injury.

Abbott maybe the worst of all the candidates endorsed by the Teamsters this year, but it’s a ghoul’s list to choose from, including the anti-Woke, anti-union Vivek Ramaswamy for Governor of Ohio, to the fanatical Israel supporter Rep. Mike Lawler of New York, to insider trader Rep. Rob Bresnahan of Pennsylvania to Rep. Max Miller accused of spousal and child abuse. O’Brien personally endorsed Lawler at a rally in New York, and hosted him, Bresnahan, and Ramaswamy on his little-watched podcast Better Bad Ideas. All of them have low, life-time scores for voting on pro-union legislation calculated by the AFL-CIO and each one went down to defeat on November third.

However, it was O’Brien’s endorsement of Florida’s junior U.S. Senator Ashley Moody that really irked many people, who don’t normally pay attention to Teamster politics. He announced on X, “Teamsters General President Sean O’Brien here. Just voted in the State of Florida for the first time, and very proud to have cast a ballot for @SenAshleyMoody.” Moody was appointed by Republican Governor Ron DeSantis to replace Marco Rubio in the U.S. Senate following his confirmation as Secretary of State by President Donald Trump in 2025. Moody had been DeSantis’ Attorney General doing his dirty work. Journalist Hamilton Nolan wrote recently:

Ashley Moody was the attorney general of Florida under Ron Desantis. She supported the vicious anti-union state laws that Ron Desantis has passed — which aim to destroy public sector union membership in the state. She, in fact, personally defended those union-busting laws in court and filed a lawsuit against the Biden administration for trying to push back on them. (She also joined a Republican lawsuit trying to overturn the 2020 election results, helped to funnel $10 million intended for children’s health care into right wing political efforts, and pushed Covid conspiracies, among other nice things.)

In sharp contrast, “Moody’s Democratic opponent Angie Nixon, who Sean O’Brien did not vote for, is a former union organizer who has personally walked Teamsters picket lines alongside Sean O’Brien.” Nixon joined the Democratic Socialist of America (DSA) in June 2026, another in a growing list of DSA candidates or supported candidates or the left in general attacked by O’Brien. She responded to O’Brien, “Ashley Moody NEVER walked the line with you @TeamsterSOB. But, ok brother. Shout out to all of the rank & file Teamsters that are voting for me. I will ALWAYS STAND WITH YOU!” Moody won by a bare majority of 50.8% of the vote to Nixon’s 48%. Could a Teamster endorsement of Nixon make a difference? Possibly.

Hamilton Nolan was one of first writers on the left to forefront the disastrous Teamsters’ endorsements. He wrote:

Sean O’Brien is an idiot. Let us count the ways, from petty to substantial. As a native Floridian, I am quite familiar with the “rich Yankee testosterone guy who moves to Florida and votes Republican.” The state is crawling with these clowns. Generally they congregate in gaudy cigar bars and on pleasure boats, so it’s easy to stay away from them, but their negative effect on state politics is harder to avoid. I am also familiar with the compulsion of aging men to post clips of themselves working out and doing ostentatiously tough guy stuff. As men, we struggle against our own mortality by being macho, rather than by having “emotional intelligence” or whatever. Testosterone is a powerful and dangerous drug.

I really agree with Nolan on this. The highest levels of the decision making body of the Teamsters have been captured by the sad, pathetic, bloviating, and far right manosphere. They would be comical, if they weren’t so incompetent, if not outright dangerous. O’Brien appears to have believed that Trump’s re-election in 2024 was a permanent realignment of U.S. politics and he would pursue a self-serving strategy at the expense of the rest of the working class. While he claims to pursue a political strategy that is “bipartisan” or “not beholden to anyone or a party” as he embraced the far right, and it’s blown up in his face.

Yet, the problem runs much deeper than that. The Teamsters recent convention saw O’Brien and his supporters elected by 96% of the delegates. It was the first since 1991 that there wasn’t a rank and file election to elect the top officers of the union. A conservative and bloated bureaucracy earning multiple salaries dominates the union, that on local and state wide is beholden to the other party of big business: the Democrats. The immediate issue is how long can the reformers and the left inside and outside the Teamsters allow Sean O’Brien to pursue his dangerous liaison with the far right?

Joe Allen is a former Teamster. He has written for Counterpunch, Rebel, Tempest, Jacobin, Socialist Worker, and the International Socialist Review.

title: Motown and the Making of Working-Class Revolutionaries: an Interview with Jerome Scott and Walda Katz-Fishman (UAWD Daily Struggle)
content:
Anthony Stoner October 26, 2026

Jerome Scott and Walda Katz-Fishman, authors of Motown and the Making of Working-Class Revolutionaries: The League of Revolutionary Black Workers, share their reflections on the UAW’s Black radical tradition, the tactic of the wildcat strike, and the importance of unions fighting for the working class as a whole.

In the 1960s, Chrysler—the only Big Three corporation whose operations remained largely in Detroit at the time—began to hire Black workers, many fresh from the U.S. South. They had the worst and most dangerous jobs, and Chrysler frequently fired them before they obtained UAW contract protections after a 90-day probation. In 1968, these conditions and the lack of representation by the white-dominated UAW—at that time led by Walter Reuther, whose “Administration Caucus” dominated the union then and for decades after his death led to a wildcat strike in the Dodge Main plant initiated by the Dodge Revolutionary Union Movement (DRUM) (A wildcat strike is a strike not officially authorized by a union). A number of other RUMs were then created around Detroit, and in 1969 the League of Revolutionary Black Workers (LRBW) was founded by Black militant labor organizers to help unite and aid struggles around the city.
